title: Catch an ImportError
description:
Source instruction (Exercises: Day 15, item 1): "Open you python interactive shell and try all the examples covered in this section."

ImportError example: `from math import power` raises `ImportError: cannot import name 'power' from 'math'` ("There is no function called power in the math module, it goes with a different name: pow"); fixed by `from math import pow` then `pow(2, 3)` which returns `8.0`.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `safe_from_import(code)`, executing the given `from ... import ...` statement (optionally followed by a line assigning to `result`) and returning the value bound to `result` (or "OK" if none was assigned), or a string "ImportError: <message>" if the import itself fails.
examples:
safe_from_import("from math import power") -> "ImportError: cannot import name 'power' from 'math' (unknown location)"
safe_from_import("from math import pow\nresult = pow(2, 3)") -> 8.0
hints: A `from module import name` statement raises ImportError (not AttributeError) when name doesn't exist in module, so run the given code string with exec() to trigger the real error.
Give exec() its own local namespace dict so you can read back any variables the executed code assigns, such as a `result = ...` line.

Wrap the exec(code, {}, local_ns) call in try/except ImportError, and in the except branch return an f-string starting with 'ImportError: ' followed by the caught exception object; otherwise return local_ns.get('result', 'OK').
expected_behavior: Executes the given code string (a from-import, optionally followed by a `result = ...` line) in its own namespace. If it runs successfully, returns the value bound to `result`, or "OK" if nothing was assigned. If the from-import raises an ImportError, catches it and returns a descriptive string in the form "ImportError: <message>" instead of letting the exception propagate.

hidden_tests.label: no 'power' name in math, mirrors the source example
valid import and call, mirrors the source's fix

explanation: A `from module import name` statement raises ImportError when the module exists but has no attribute with that name - `power` doesn't exist in math (it's called `pow`), so `from math import power` raises ImportError, which is caught and turned into a descriptive string. exec() with an explicit namespace lets the function read back any value the executed code assigns to `result`.
